tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

**Goal:** Turn user intent into a hardened, reviewable artifact.

**CRITICAL:** If a step directs you to another snapshot file, read it fully and follow it. No exceptions.

Subagents, when the capability is available, are an important part of this workflow. Use them as directed by the workflow steps.
If you need an explicit user instruction to run them, ask once now for the whole workflow run.

## READY FOR DEVELOPMENT STANDARD

A specification is "Ready for Development" when:

- **Actionable**: Every task has a file path and specific action.
- **Logical**: Tasks ordered by dependency.
- **Testable**: All ACs use Given/When/Then.
- **Complete**: No placeholders or TBDs.
- **Sufficient**: No known requirement, acceptance, dependency, or implementation gaps remain unresolved.
- **Coherent**: No unresolved ambiguities or internal contradictions.

## SCOPE STANDARD

A specification should target a **single user-facing goal** within **900–1600 tokens**:

- **Single goal**: One cohesive feature, even if it spans multiple layers/files. Multi-goal means >=2 **top-level independent shippable deliverables** — each could be reviewed, tested, and merged as a separate PR without breaking the others. Never count surface verbs, "and" conjunctions, or noun phrases. Never split cross-layer implementation details inside one user goal.
  - Split: "add dark mode toggle AND refactor auth to JWT AND build admin dashboard"
  - Don't split: "add validation and display errors" / "support drag-and-drop AND paste AND retry"
- **900–1600 tokens**: Optimal range for LLM consumption. Below 900 risks ambiguity; above 1600 risks context-rot in implementation agents.
- **Neither limit is a gate.** Both are proposals with user override.

## Conventions

- Every operational cross-file reference in this workflow is an absolute snapshot path. Open it directly; do not resolve it relative to a skill directory.
- `{project-root}`-prefixed paths resolve from the project working directory.

# Epic 5 Context: Semantic Search & Filtering

<!-- Compiled from planning artifacts. Edit freely. Regenerate with compile-epic-context if planning docs change. -->

## Goal

Users can find any Entry again by meaning rather than exact keyword match, and narrow results by source and date range, with search input debounced and filter-clearing restoring the full list without a reload. This epic realizes journey UJ-4 (finding a past entry by meaning, then narrowing with filters) and depends on Epic 4's timeline screen (Meus Registros) as the surface search and filtering mount onto. It extends the same `EntriesRepository` port Epic 3 introduced with `list`/`search` capabilities — it introduces no second Entry model — but stands as its own epic because it is its own user-facing milestone, not a structural completion of Epic 4's job.

## Stories

- Story 5.1: Semantic Search with Debounced Input
- Story 5.2: Metadata Filters
- Story 5.3: Combined Search + Filter & Non-Disruptive Clearing

## Requirements & Constraints

- Search is meaning-based, not literal: a query for one word must surface entries that only use a semantically related word, never requiring exact text match.
- Search input is debounced 300ms client-side before any request fires — the backend performs no throttling of its own, so the debounce is entirely the app's responsibility.
- Filtering is limited to source (manual/audio/photo/chat) and date range (`dateFrom`/`dateTo`) only. There is no tag/category filter anywhere — tags exist only as a read-only, embedded field on an Entry (populated by seed data, never user-created or filterable).
- Filtering with no active search term queries the plain entries-list; filtering combined with an active search term queries the semantic-search endpoint, carrying the same filter parameters. Multiple simultaneous filters (and a search term, when present) combine with AND semantics only — never OR.
- Clearing active filters restores the full unfiltered list in place, without a full screen reload or re-mount.
- The app is cloud-only: offline permits viewing already-cached entries but never writing. After a reconnect, the local cache must stay duplicate-free — no entry appears twice.
- A loading indicator appears only once a request exceeds ~300ms; faster responses show no loading UI at all.

## Technical Decisions

- Call the backend only via its function name, never the literal REST path: entries-list at `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/entries-list` (used for `GET /entries` with `source`/`dateFrom`/`dateTo`/`cursor`/`limit`) and entries-search at `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/entries-search` (used for `GET /entries/search` with `q`/`source`/`dateFrom`/`dateTo`/`limit`, capped at 50). Note entries-search has **no** `cursor` parameter — unlike entries-list, it is not paginated.
- Extend the existing `EntriesRepository` port (owned by `entries/domain`, introduced in Epic 3) with `list` and `search` methods; the port still exposes create and read only in spirit — no update/delete is ever added, and no second Entry model is created for search results.
- Offline carve-out: semantic search has no client-side vector index, so a search attempted offline resolves immediately to `Failure.networkOffline`, exactly like a write — it is never served from the local cache. Plain filtered list reads, by contrast, may still fall back to the cached Hive box.
- Every query dimension (source, date range, the search term itself) must be a server-side query parameter; the Hive box continues to store exactly what the server returned, keyed by id — no local filtering, joining, sorting, or re-deriving of the cached collection is ever implemented client-side.
- Screens in this epic that are single-data-source, single-fetch-lifecycle use the shared generic `Resource<T>` (`idle`/`loading`/`data`/`error`) state wrapper from `core/`, rather than defining a feature-specific sealed state class.
- Repository methods still return `Either<Failure, T>`, consistent with the rest of the app's resilience contract.

## UX & Interaction Patterns

- Search bar: paper-elevated input with a trailing funnel icon, permanently docked at the top of Meus Registros; it is never submitted via a button — only the debounced live query matters.
- Filter chips: sage background, dark-olive text, fully rounded. Single-choice (date range) and multi-choice (source) filters look visually identical and differ only in underlying behavior.
- Filter sheet: a `radiusLg`/`elevation2` bottom sheet with filter groups labeled in the mono-caption text style.
- Representative flow from the design walkthrough: a user searches "ansiedade" and sees results that only mention a related word ("nervosismo"); she then opens the filter sheet and narrows to a date range plus the audio source, and results re-narrow with AND logic.
- Entrance choreography is limited to the two system-wide animations (`sheetUp` for the bottom sheet, `scrimIn` for any scrim) — no other motion is introduced.
- Filter chips and the search/filter surfaces are a tight-fit area for Dynamic Type — verify text does not truncate or clip at the largest accessibility size.

## Cross-Story Dependencies

- Depends on Epic 4: search and filtering operate over the Meus Registros timeline screen and the entries Hive cache Epic 4 already built; there is nothing to search or filter before that exists.
- Depends on Epic 3's `EntriesRepository` port (introduced under `entries/domain`) being extended here rather than replaced — Story 5.1/5.2 add `search`/`list` capabilities to that one existing port.
- Story 5.3 depends on both 5.1 (search) and 5.2 (filters) being in place, since it is specifically the combined-query and clearing behavior layered on top of both.

---
title: 'Metadata Filters'
type: 'feature'
created: '2026-11-05'
status: 'done'
review_loop_iteration: 1
context: []
baseline_commit: '6e4e9d5e37f376592cb6491f0132ecd052511bc0'
---

<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** Meus Registros' funnel button is a no-op (spec-5-1) — there is no way to narrow the plain timeline by entry source or date range, and `EntriesRepository.list()` has no filter parameters to call.

**Approach:** Extend `list()` with `source`/`dateFrom`/`dateTo`; add a filter bottom sheet and a removable active-filter-chip row to `MeusRegistrosCubit`'s existing plain-timeline branch. Filters apply only to the unfiltered list path this story — combining them with an active search term is story 5.3.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- `EntriesRepository.list({String? cursor, int limit = 20, EntrySource? source, DateTime? dateFrom, DateTime? dateTo})`; `EntriesRemoteDataSource.list()` forwards non-null values as `source`(`.name`)/`dateFrom`/`dateTo` (ISO-8601) to `entries-list`, mirroring `search()`'s existing convention.
- Source is single-choice (`EntrySource?`, not a `Set`) — see Design Notes.
- `MeusRegistrosCubit` gains `applyFilters({source, dateFrom, dateTo})`/`clearFilters()` (own methods, not `loadFirstPage()` — see Design Notes); both bump `_generation`, replace state via `list()`. `_fetchMore()` carries active filters forward alongside `cursor`.
- `_offlineFallback()` stays as-is (full unfiltered box dump, same `cursor == null` trigger) — offline + filters silently returns the full cached list (AD-9: cache is never locally filtered).
- New `EntriesFilterSheet` + static `.show()`, mirroring `InsertionModal.show()`'s pattern (`isScrollControlled`, `useSafeArea`, `colorScrimHeavy`, Reduce-Motion-aware `durationSheetUp`). Groups: "INTERVALO DE DATA" (Todo o período/Esta semana/Este mês → computed `dateFrom`/`dateTo`) and "TIPO DE ENTRADA" (manual/áudio/foto/chat), both single-choice. No "CATEGORIA". "Aplicar" commits via `cubit.applyFilters(...)` + closes; "Limpar" resets only the sheet's pending selection.
- Active-filters chip row renders under the search bar, only inside the existing `ResourceIdle` branch (`meus_registros_screen.dart:209`), when any filter is active; each chip removable ("x", re-applies the rest); "Limpar filtros" link calls `cubit.clearFilters()`. Chips: `colorSecondary`/`colorCategoryChipText`/`radiusFull`.
- `EntriesSearchBar` gains `onFilterTap` (replaces `onPressed: () {}`, line 63) and `hasActiveFilters` (fills the funnel icon).

**Ask First:** none — scope pinned by `epic-5-context.md` and RF06.

**Never:** filter params on `EntriesSearchCubit`/`search()`, or a combined search+filter query (story 5.3); a "CATEGORIA"/tag group (extension, forbidden); client-side filtering/sorting of the cached box; a new cubit/DI registration.

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Source filter only | Aplicar with "áudio" selected | query `source=audio`; results narrowed | N/A |
| Source + date range together | both selected, Aplicar | one query, both params — AND narrowing | N/A |
| Remove one of two active chips | tap "x" on the source chip | re-queries with only the date range | N/A |
| Clear all filters | "Limpar filtros" link tapped | full unfiltered list restored in place, no reload/re-mount | N/A |
| Load more with filters active | scroll to bottom, filters active | `_fetchMore` sends `cursor` + same filters | N/A |
| Offline, filters active, first page | no connectivity | `_offlineFallback()`'s full unfiltered cached dump renders, no error shown | N/A (cache content silently ignores filters, per AD-9) |

</frozen-after-approval>

## Code Map

- `entries_repository.dart:38` -- `list()` signature to extend
- `entries_remote_data_source.dart:54-61` -- query-param building to extend
- `entries_repository_impl.dart:55-95` (`list()`), `:189-208` (`_offlineFallback()`, stays filter-oblivious)
- `meus_registros_cubit.dart:58` (`_generation`), `:138-140` (`loadFirstPage()`), `:223-225` (`_fetchMore()`)
- `meus_registros_screen.dart:198` (search bar docking), `:201-237` (`ResourceIdle` fork — chip row + sheet mount here)
- `entries_search_bar.dart:19,58-72` -- funnel no-op to replace with `onFilterTap`/`hasActiveFilters`
- `insertion_modal.dart:63-135` -- bottom-sheet `.show()` pattern to mirror
- `entry.dart:6` -- `EntrySource` enum (manual/audio/photo/chat), confirmed no `tags` field to touch
- `design_tokens.dart` -- reuse `colorSecondary`/`colorCategoryChipText`/`radiusFull`/`radiusLg`/`elevation2`/`textMonoCaption`/`durationSheetUp`/`colorScrimHeavy`; no new token

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**
- [x] `entries_repository.dart` -- add `source`/`dateFrom`/`dateTo` params to `list()`
- [x] `entries_remote_data_source.dart` -- forward new params as query params to `entries-list`
- [x] `entries_repository_impl.dart` -- pass params through; leave `_offlineFallback()` untouched
- [x] `meus_registros_cubit.dart` -- add `applyFilters()`/`clearFilters()`; carry filters into `_fetchMore()`
- [x] `presentation/widgets/entries_filter_sheet.dart` (new) -- date-range + source groups, Aplicar/Limpar
- [x] `entries_search_bar.dart` -- `onFilterTap` + `hasActiveFilters` (filled icon)
- [x] `meus_registros_screen.dart` -- wire sheet trigger; render active-filter chip row in the `ResourceIdle` branch
- [x] Unit tests covering every I/O Matrix row across the new/changed files
- [x] Widget tests: filter sheet (selection, Aplicar/Limpar), chip row (remove one, clear all), filled funnel icon

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given the filter sheet, when "áudio" + a date range are both applied, then the single `entries-list` query carries both params and results narrow with AND logic.
- Given active filters, when "Limpar filtros" is tapped, then the full unfiltered list renders in place without a screen reload or re-mount.
- Given active filters, when the user scrolls to load more, then the continuation request carries the same filters alongside `cursor`.
- Given the device is offline with filters active on the first page, when the fallback fires, then it shows the full cached list, not a filtered or empty one.

### Review Findings

**Patch:**
- [x] [Review][Patch] `dateFrom`/`dateTo` were sent via `.toIso8601String()` on local (non-UTC) `DateTime`s, which omits the `Z`/offset the OpenAPI contract's `format: date-time` (RFC3339) requires. [lib/features/entries/data/datasources/entries_remote_data_source.dart:78-79] — fixed: serialize via `.toUtc().toIso8601String()` at the serialization boundary only.
- [x] [Review][Patch] A newly-created/pending entry was prepended into the filtered list unconditionally, visibly violating an active filter. [lib/features/entries/presentation/cubit/meus_registros_cubit.dart] — fixed: added `_matchesActiveFilters()`/`_visiblePendingWrites`, gating both the confirmed-entry prepend and the pending-write placeholder on the active filter.
- [x] [Review][Patch] The funnel's "filled" (active-filters) indicator stayed on during unrelated search results. [lib/features/entries/presentation/screens/meus_registros_screen.dart:208] — fixed: gated on `searchState is ResourceIdle<List<Entry>>` too.
- [x] [Review][Patch] The error-state "Tentar novamente" button called `loadFirstPage()`, which resets active filters before retrying — a failed filtered query silently "succeeded" with the full unfiltered list instead. [lib/features/entries/presentation/screens/meus_registros_screen.dart:233] — fixed: added `MeusRegistrosCubit.retryCurrentPage()` (keeps the active filter selection), wired to `onRetry` instead.
- [x] [Review][Patch] `dateRangePresetMatching()` checked `thisWeek` before `thisMonth`, mislabeling a month-long filter as "Esta semana" whenever the month's 1st coincides with that Monday. [lib/features/entries/presentation/widgets/entries_filter_sheet.dart] — fixed: check order swapped; the separate staleness-after-rollover limitation is left as a known, documented tradeoff.
- [x] [Review][Patch] No Dynamic Type/accessibility-scaling test existed for the new `EntriesFilterSheet`, despite its own doc citing epic-5's explicit UX note. [test/features/entries/presentation/widgets/entries_filter_sheet_test.dart] — fixed: added a `TextScaler.linear(3.0)` test.
- [x] [Review][Patch] No screen-level test exercised two active-filter chips rendered together or the date-range chip's own "x". [test/features/entries/presentation/screens/meus_registros_screen_test.dart] — fixed: added a source+date-range test tapping the date-range chip's removal specifically.
- [x] [Review][Patch] `EntriesFilterSheet.show()`'s reduce-motion branch had no test, unlike `InsertionModal`'s equivalent. [test/features/entries/presentation/widgets/entries_filter_sheet_test.dart] — fixed: added a reduce-motion test mirroring `insertion_modal_test.dart`'s pattern.

**Reject (noise, dropped):** offline+filters silently showing the unfiltered cache is an explicit, already-frozen Boundary (AD-9), not a bug; the funnel staying tappable during an active search is inert by design (updates hidden cubit state with no visible effect until search clears); "date-range boundary inclusivity" isn't testable client-side since the app only forwards `dateFrom`/`dateTo` verbatim — inclusivity is the backend's own contract behavior.

### Review Findings (round 2)

**Patch (round 2):**
- [x] [Review][Patch] [Decision: resolved — exempt live entries] `DateRangePreset.rangeFrom()` freezes `dateTo` to `DateTime.now()` at the moment "Aplicar" is tapped (Design Notes: "dateTo is always now itself"), and the code-review-fix guard `_matchesActiveFilters()` rejects any `occurredAt` that `isAfter(_activeDateTo!)`. Since a freshly-created entry's `occurredAt` is by definition after the filter's apply-time, every entry created after applying "Esta semana"/"Este mês" was permanently excluded from view for as long as that filter stayed active — deterministic, not a rare timing coincidence, and silent. [lib/features/entries/presentation/cubit/meus_registros_cubit.dart:93-105 (`_matchesActiveFilters`)] — `docs/input/` is silent on this exact interaction (AGENTS.md: "decide and proceed"); resolved in favor of consistency with every other filter dimension in this cubit (new entries show live unless they actually violate the filter) — fix: the local live-match guard no longer enforces the `dateTo` upper bound at all (a freshly-created entry's `occurredAt` is always "now", so it can never meaningfully exceed a `dateTo` that only makes sense as a server-query narrowing bound); `dateTo` keeps narrowing the server `list()` query exactly as before — only the local overlay check changes. Secondary, same root cause: `_matchesActiveFilters()`'s `dateFrom` lower-bound check remains a client-side inclusivity assumption (`isBefore`, i.e. inclusive-at-the-boundary) that could still disagree with the backend's own real narrowing for an entry landing exactly on the lower boundary — accepted as a pre-existing, out-of-scope limitation (same rationale as the spec's own already-frozen boundary-inclusivity Reject note), since it only affects the local overlay's instant-visibility signal and the next full reload still shows the server's authoritative answer.
- [x] [Review][Patch] `dateRangePresetMatching()` re-derives the active date-range preset from `_activeDateFrom` by exact-equality match against a freshly recomputed "today" boundary. Once a day/week/month boundary rolls over while a date filter stays active (the filter is session-scoped and outlives any single day), reopening `EntriesFilterSheet` mis-pre-selects "Todo o período" instead of the still-active preset, and tapping "Aplicar" with nothing touched then calls `rangeFrom()` on that wrong preset, resolving to `(null, null)` — silently clearing the still-active date filter. The active-filter chip row mislabels the same way (shows "Todo o período" while a date filter is still narrowing every query). [lib/features/entries/presentation/widgets/entries_filter_sheet.dart:44-85 (`DateRangePreset.rangeFrom`, `dateRangePresetMatching`), :167-175 (`_EntriesFilterSheetState.initState`), lib/features/entries/presentation/screens/meus_registros_screen.dart:~691 (chip label)] — suggested fix: store the selected `DateRangePreset` itself as an explicit field on `MeusRegistrosCubit` (alongside `_activeDateFrom`/`_activeDateTo`, set directly by `applyFilters()`/`clearFilters()`/`loadFirstPage()`), and have both the sheet's `initState` and the chip label read it directly instead of re-deriving it from `dateFrom`.
- [x] [Review][Patch] No screen-level (widget) test verifies that `_ErrorState`'s "Tentar novamente" button — rewired from `loadFirstPage` to `retryCurrentPage()` specifically so a failed *filtered* query retries with the same filter rather than silently falling back to the full unfiltered list — actually preserves an active filter when tapped through the real UI. The existing cubit test calls `retryCurrentPage()` directly (bypassing the screen's wiring entirely); the one widget test that taps the real button never has a filter active, where `loadFirstPage()`/`retryCurrentPage()` are behaviorally identical. A regression reverting `onRetry` back to `loadFirstPage` would go undetected by either test. [test/features/entries/presentation/screens/meus_registros_screen_test.dart] — suggested fix: add a case mirroring the existing "load failure renders retry" test, but with a filter applied first, a queued failure, a tap on "Tentar novamente", and an assertion that the retried call still carries the active filter.
- [x] [Review][Patch] The funnel icon's `tooltip` is the unconditional literal `'Filtros'` regardless of `hasActiveFilters` — a screen-reader user has no way to learn filters are currently applied without separately discovering the active-filter chip row. [lib/features/entries/presentation/widgets/entries_search_bar.dart] — suggested fix: `tooltip: hasActiveFilters ? 'Filtros (ativos)' : 'Filtros'` (or equivalent).
- [x] [Review][Patch] No test exercises "date range filter only" applied from a clean, no-filter starting state — the one existing date-only assertion is reached by removing the source chip from an already-combined filter, not a from-scratch date-only `applyFilters()` call, leaving "Source filter only"'s own dedicated I/O-matrix row asymmetric with its date-only counterpart. [test/features/entries/presentation/cubit/meus_registros_cubit_test.dart]
- [x] [Review][Patch] No cubit-level unit test removes the *date-range* chip while keeping *source* active — only the reverse direction (removing source, keeping date range) is tested at the cubit level (`meus_registros_cubit_test.dart:771-794`); the date-chip-removal direction is covered only at the screen widget-test level, so a regression isolated to the cubit's own `applyFilters(source: source)` call path could ship undetected by the cubit suite alone. [test/features/entries/presentation/cubit/meus_registros_cubit_test.dart]
- [x] [Review][Patch] `EntriesFilterSheet`'s reopen-preselection round-trip test only exercises the "Este mês" preset through the sheet's actual `initState`/reopen flow; "Esta semana" is tested only against the bare `dateRangePresetMatching()` function directly (`entries_filter_sheet_test.dart:338-348`), never through the real reopen wiring, leaving that pre-selection path's actual wiring for "Esta semana" unverified end-to-end. [test/features/entries/presentation/widgets/entries_filter_sheet_test.dart]
- [x] [Review][Patch] No `test-summary.md` entry exists for story 5-2-metadata-filters — breaks the pattern every prior story (4.3, 4.4, 5.1) in this repo followed; this diff's `tests/test-summary.md` changes are entirely about closing out story 5.1's round-2 patch. [_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/tests/test-summary.md]
- [x] [Review][Patch] No test exercises the ordering where a confirmed/pending item is already visible under "no active filter" and `applyFilters()` is then called while it's still outstanding, verifying it correctly drops out of view once it no longer matches the newly-applied filter — every existing "must never violate the active filter" test applies the filter first and has the item arrive afterward, never the reverse order. Code-reading confirms this is structurally safe by construction (`_loadFiltered()` fully replaces `entries`/`pendingWrites` from a fresh server-filtered page plus `_visiblePendingWrites` on every filter change, so no separate incremental path could drift) — this is a coverage gap, not a known live bug. [test/features/entries/presentation/cubit/meus_registros_cubit_test.dart]

**Defer:**
- [x] [Review][Defer] The round-2 fix for story 5.1 bundled into this same commit (`MeusRegistrosScreen.initState` arming `_searchSkeletonTimer` when `EntriesSearchCubit` is already `ResourceLoading` at remount) always starts a fresh 300ms timer regardless of how long the search has already been loading — a remount after the search has been loading well past the threshold still waits up to another full 300ms before showing the skeleton. [lib/features/entries/presentation/screens/meus_registros_screen.dart:96-105] — deferred: a complete fix needs `EntriesSearchCubit` (story 5.1, already `done`) to expose a `loadingStartedAt` timestamp, which is out of this story's own scope; the consequence is a sub-300ms cosmetic delay in an already-narrow remount-while-loading scenario, not a correctness issue.

**Reject (noise, dropped — round 2):** `EntriesFilterSheet`'s "Aplicar" always re-triggers `_loadFiltered()`'s network round-trip even when the pending selection is unchanged from what's already active — correct result either way, no AC requires short-circuiting it, and adding one would be unrequested scope; a large fraction of this diff's test-file hunks are pure dart-format reflow of pre-existing tests with no behavioral change mixed into the functional diff — a review-process observation, not a code defect; `hasActiveFilters`/`activeSource`/etc. being plain getters on the cubit rather than carried on `MeusRegistrosState` means `EntriesSearchBar` rebuilds on every unrelated `MeusRegistrosCubit` emission (e.g. each `loadMore()` page) — real but purely a rebuild-efficiency nitpick on a cheap, pure `StatelessWidget`, with no visible or correctness impact.

## Design Notes

TIPO DE ENTRADA is single-choice, not multi-choice as the prototype's chip row suggests: `source` (openapi.yaml, both endpoints) accepts exactly one enum value, and AD-9 forbids merging multiple per-source queries client-side — the prototype is a visual reference, not an API contract, so the frozen backend wins.

`applyFilters()`/`clearFilters()` are separate from `loadFirstPage()` because that method's doc contract is "always re-fetch on mount" — reusing it for an in-session filter change would conflate two different triggers.

1	import 'package:fpdart/fpdart.dart';
2	
3	import '../../../../core/failure/failure.dart';
4	import '../entities/entries_page.dart';
5	import '../entities/entry.dart';
6	
7	/// The port later epics extend (Code Map) — `features/capture/` depends on
8	/// this abstract class only, never `entries/data` or `entries/presentation`
9	/// (RNF06).
10	abstract class EntriesRepository {
11	  /// Posts to `entries-create` (`ApiClient.post`, via
12	  /// `EntriesRemoteDataSource`) and, on success, writes the entry through
13	  /// to the `entries` Hive box before returning `Right` (Boundaries) — a
14	  /// caller that only reads the returned [Entry] never needs to touch the
15	  /// box itself. Every [Failure] — including
16	  /// [Failure.networkOffline] — is returned as `Left`, unmapped and
17	  /// un-retried; the caller decides what to do with it (RNF09).
18	  Future<Either<Failure, Entry>> create({
19	    required String content,
20	    required EntrySource source,
21	    int? mediaDurationSeconds,
22	  });
23	
24	  /// Calls `entries-list` (`ApiClient.get`, via
25	  /// `EntriesRemoteDataSource`), newest-first by `occurredAt` — server
26	  /// behavior assumed, undocumented (Code Map, decided per AGENTS.md
27	  /// policy: "where `docs/input/` is silent... decide and proceed").
28	  ///
29	  /// spec-5-2 — [source]/[dateFrom]/[dateTo] are forwarded to
30	  /// `entries-list` as its own `source`/`dateFrom`/`dateTo` query
31	  /// parameters (`EntriesRemoteDataSource.list()`'s own doc), each only
32	  /// when non-null; combining more than one narrows with AND logic (the
33	  /// backend's own semantics, RF06 Acceptance Criteria) — this repository
34	  /// does no client-side filtering/joining of its own (AD-9).
35	  ///
36	  /// On [Failure.networkOffline]/[Failure.networkTimeout] specifically,
37	  /// falls back to a full dump of the `entries` Hive box, sorted
38	  /// `occurredAt` desc, with `EntriesPage.nextCursor: null` (Boundaries) —
39	  /// every *other* [Failure] (e.g. [Failure.authExpired]) propagates as
40	  /// `Left`, unmapped (RNF09). That fallback (`cursor == null` only) stays
41	  /// filter-oblivious regardless of [source]/[dateFrom]/[dateTo] — AD-9:
42	  /// the cache is never locally filtered, so an offline first page always
43	  /// renders the full cached list even with filters active.
44	  ///
45	  /// A successful page persists every item to the `entries` Hive box
46	  /// *before* returning `Right` — same "persist then return" ordering
47	  /// [create] already uses.
48	  Future<Either<Failure, EntriesPage>> list({
49	    String? cursor,
50	    int limit = 20,
51	    EntrySource? source,
52	    DateTime? dateFrom,
53	    DateTime? dateTo,
54	  });
55	
56	  /// spec-4-4 (RF07) — calls `entries-get` (`ApiClient.get`, via
57	  /// `EntriesRemoteDataSource`) with [id] as the one path parameter, then
58	  /// persists the fetched entry to the `entries` Hive box (`put`) *before*
59	  /// returning `Right` — same "persist then return" ordering
60	  /// [create]/[list] already use. AD-11 keeps this port create+read-only,
61	  /// not count-capped — [search] (spec-5-1) added a fourth method without
62	  /// contradicting that.
63	  ///
64	  /// On [Failure.networkOffline]/[Failure.networkTimeout] specifically,
65	  /// falls back to `entriesBox.get(id)` if present; a cache miss propagates
66	  /// the original failure unchanged (no synthesized not-found — that
67	  /// distinction belongs to whichever `Failure` the backend/network
68	  /// actually produced). Every *other* [Failure] — including
69	  /// [Failure.notFound] for an id that never existed or belongs to another
70	  /// user — is returned as `Left`, unmapped (RNF09); RNF04 (identical
71	  /// treatment for both causes) is the caller's own rendering job, never
72	  /// this repository's.
73	  Future<Either<Failure, Entry>> getById(String id);
74	
75	  /// spec-5-1 — calls `entries-search` (`ApiClient.get`, via
76	  /// `EntriesRemoteDataSource`) with [query] as the one `q` query
77	  /// parameter (no `limit`/`cursor` — Boundaries). [query] is always
78	  /// already a non-empty, pre-trimmed string by the time it reaches this
79	  /// method — `EntriesSearchCubit` owns that guarantee, never this
80	  /// repository.
81	  ///
82	  /// On success, persists every returned entry to the `entries` Hive box
83	  /// (`putAll`) *before* returning `Right` — same "persist then return"
84	  /// ordering [list]/[getById] already use. Unlike [list]/[getById], there
85	  /// is no offline/timeout cache fallback here (AD-9: no client-side
86	  /// vector index) — every [Failure], including
87	  /// [Failure.networkOffline], is returned as `Left`, unmapped (RNF09).
88	  Future<Either<Failure, List<Entry>>> search(String query);
89	}

1	import 'dart:async';
2	
3	import 'package:flutter_bloc/flutter_bloc.dart';
4	
5	import '../../../../core/utils/deduped_by_id.dart';
6	import '../../domain/entities/date_range_preset.dart';
7	import '../../domain/entities/entry.dart';
8	import '../../domain/entities/pending_entry_write.dart';
9	import '../../domain/repositories/entries_repository.dart';
10	import '../../domain/services/pending_entry_write_tracker.dart';
11	import 'meus_registros_state.dart';
12	
13	/// Drives `MeusRegistrosScreen` — calls `EntriesRepository.list()` directly
14	/// (no use-case layer, matching this codebase's existing small-scope
15	/// convention: `AccountSettingsCubit`/`AuthCubit`/`TextEntryCubit`). A
16	/// `lazySingleton` (Code Map), like `AccountSettingsCubit` — long-lived, so
17	/// the already-fetched pages survive leaving and re-entering
18	/// `/meus-registros` within the same app session.
19	///
20	/// spec-4-2 — also subscribes to [PendingEntryWriteTracker.pendingWrites]/
21	/// `.confirmedWrites` for this cubit's whole lifetime (constructor-wired,
22	/// not `loadFirstPage()`-wired): both streams are shared singleton
23	/// broadcasts a capture cubit on a *different* screen can drive at any
24	/// time, and this cubit is itself a long-lived singleton that must reflect
25	/// them regardless of which screen is currently visible.
26	class MeusRegistrosCubit extends Cubit<MeusRegistrosState> {
27	  MeusRegistrosCubit(this._repository, this._tracker)
28	    : super(const MeusRegistrosLoading()) {
29	    _pendingSubscription = _tracker.pendingWrites.listen(
30	      _onPendingWritesChanged,
31	    );
32	    _confirmedSubscription = _tracker.confirmedWrites.listen(_onEntryConfirmed);
33	  }
34	
35	  final EntriesRepository _repository;
36	  final PendingEntryWriteTracker _tracker;
37	  late final StreamSubscription<List<PendingEntryWrite>> _pendingSubscription;
38	  late final StreamSubscription<({String tempId, Entry entry})>
39	  _confirmedSubscription;
40	
41	  /// Mirrors the tracker's own latest snapshot regardless of [state]'s
42	  /// current type — so a pending write that arrives while [state] is
43	  /// still [MeusRegistrosLoading]/[MeusRegistrosError] isn't lost: the
44	  /// next [loadFirstPage] that resolves into [MeusRegistrosLoaded]/
45	  /// [MeusRegistrosEmpty] seeds itself from this field directly.
46	  List<PendingEntryWrite> _pendingWrites = const [];
47	
48	  /// A monotonic counter guarding against a stale in-flight call's result
49	  /// landing after a newer call has already changed the state (e.g. the
50	  /// user leaves and quickly re-enters `/meus-registros` while a slow
51	  /// first request is still pending, or taps retry before the original
52	  /// request resolves). Incremented at the start of every [loadFirstPage],
53	  /// then captured locally before each `await` in [loadFirstPage]/
54	  /// [_fetchMore] — a result whose captured generation no longer matches
55	  /// this counter by the time it resolves is discarded rather than
56	  /// emitted.
57	  int _generation = 0;
58	
59	  /// spec-5-2 — the session-scoped filter selection (Design Notes): `null`
60	  /// for each field means "no filter of that kind", never a sentinel
61	  /// value. Reset to "no filters" by [loadFirstPage] itself (a fresh
62	  /// mount always starts from the full unfiltered timeline — same
63	  /// "always re-fetches from scratch" contract that method's own doc
64	  /// already gives, extended here to the filter selection too), set by
65	  /// [applyFilters], cleared by [clearFilters], and carried forward by
66	  /// every [_fetchMore] call so a paginated continuation never silently
67	  /// drops the filters its first page was fetched with.
68	  EntrySource? _activeSource;
69	  DateTime? _activeDateFrom;
70	  DateTime? _activeDateTo;
71	
72	  /// Round-2 review fix: the [DateRangePreset] the active date range was
73	  /// actually selected from (if any), stored verbatim rather than
74	  /// re-derived from [_activeDateFrom] — a derivation-by-equality-match
75	  /// against a freshly recomputed "today" boundary goes stale the moment
76	  /// a day/week/month boundary rolls over while the filter stays active,
77	  /// mis-pre-selecting `EntriesFilterSheet`'s reopen state and mislabeling
78	  /// the active-filter chip. Defaults to [DateRangePreset.allTime] — same
79	  /// "no filter of that kind" convention [_activeDateFrom]/[_activeDateTo]
80	  /// already use, just non-nullable since [DateRangePreset] already has
81	  /// its own explicit "none" value.
82	  DateRangePreset _activeDateRangePreset = DateRangePreset.allTime;
83	
84	  /// `MeusRegistrosScreen`'s own read of the current filter selection —
85	  /// deliberately not part of [MeusRegistrosState] itself: [applyFilters]/
86	  /// [clearFilters] already re-emit a new state on every change, so
87	  /// whichever `BlocBuilder` reads these getters during its own `builder`
88	  /// callback rebuilds in lockstep with them regardless.
89	  EntrySource? get activeSource => _activeSource;
90	  DateTime? get activeDateFrom => _activeDateFrom;
91	  DateTime? get activeDateTo => _activeDateTo;
92	  DateRangePreset get activeDateRangePreset => _activeDateRangePreset;
93	
94	  /// `EntriesSearchBar.hasActiveFilters`/the active-filter chip row's own
95	  /// "is any filter active at all" check.
96	  bool get hasActiveFilters =>
97	      _activeSource != null || _activeDateFrom != null || _activeDateTo != null;
98	
99	  /// Code-review fix (spec-5-2): whether [source]/[occurredAt] would pass
100	  /// the currently active filter selection — `true` unconditionally once
101	  /// [hasActiveFilters] is false. Guards every path below that would
102	  /// otherwise prepend/show a brand-new confirmed entry or pending-write
103	  /// placeholder that doesn't actually belong in the currently filtered
104	  /// view (Review finding: "a newly-created entry bypasses the active
105	  /// filter" — e.g. saving a manual-text entry while `source: audio` is
106	  /// active must never visibly violate that filter).
107	  ///
108	  /// Round-2 review fix: deliberately does not check [_activeDateTo] —
109	  /// unlike [_activeSource]/[_activeDateFrom], `dateTo` only narrows the
110	  /// server-side `list()` query in [_loadFiltered] (`_activeDateTo` is
111	  /// passed straight through there); [occurredAt] here is always a
112	  /// brand-new local entry/pending-write whose timestamp is effectively
113	  /// "now", so enforcing a `dateTo` frozen at the moment the filter was
114	  /// applied would permanently hide every entry created afterward for as
115	  /// long as "Esta semana"/"Este mês" stayed active — silently breaking
116	  /// the "new entries always show immediately" guarantee every other
117	  /// filter path here already upholds.
118	  bool _matchesActiveFilters({
119	    required EntrySource source,
120	    required DateTime occurredAt,
121	  }) {
122	    if (_activeSource != null && source != _activeSource) {
123	      return false;
124	    }
125	    if (_activeDateFrom != null && occurredAt.isBefore(_activeDateFrom!)) {
126	      return false;
127	    }
128	    return true;
129	  }
130	
131	  /// [_pendingWrites] filtered down to the ones that actually match
132	  /// [_matchesActiveFilters] — [_pendingWrites] itself stays the tracker's
133	  /// own full, unfiltered bookkeeping (every write in flight/failed,
134	  /// regardless of the active filter), but a placeholder card for one
135	  /// that doesn't match the active filter must never render, same
136	  /// invariant a confirmed [Entry] gets below.
137	  List<PendingEntryWrite> get _visiblePendingWrites => _pendingWrites
138	      .where(
139	        (pending) => _matchesActiveFilters(
140	          source: pending.source,
141	          occurredAt: pending.startedAt,
142	        ),
143	      )
144	      .toList();
145	
146	  void _onPendingWritesChanged(List<PendingEntryWrite> pendingWrites) {
147	    _pendingWrites = pendingWrites;
148	    final visible = _visiblePendingWrites;
149	    final current = state;
150	    if (current is MeusRegistrosLoaded) {
151	      emit(current.copyWith(pendingWrites: visible));
152	    } else if ((current is MeusRegistrosEmpty ||
153	            current is MeusRegistrosError) &&
154	        visible.isNotEmpty) {
155	      // A capture save starts while this screen is showing "no entries
156	      // yet" or a load failure (Review finding: the latter previously
157	      // fell through this check entirely, silently dropping the pending
158	      // card) — its own placeholder card must still show immediately
159	      // (Acceptance Criteria), not wait for a reload. Gated on `visible`
160	      // rather than the raw `pendingWrites` (code-review fix): a pending
161	      // write that doesn't match the active filter has nothing to show
162	      // here at all.
163	      emit(
164	        MeusRegistrosLoaded(
165	          entries: const [],
166	          nextCursor: null,
167	          pendingWrites: visible,
168	        ),
169	      );
170	    }
171	    // MeusRegistrosLoading: nothing to overlay onto yet — [_pendingWrites]
172	    // above already keeps the latest snapshot, which the next
173	    // loadFirstPage() resolution reads directly.
174	  }
175	
176	  void _onEntryConfirmed(({String tempId, Entry entry}) confirmation) {
177	    final entry = confirmation.entry;
178	    // Review finding: drops this write's own pending placeholder from
179	    // this cubit's *local* record synchronously with prepending the
180	    // confirmed entry, in the very same handler — the tracker's own
181	    // `pendingWrites` stream will also eventually deliver the matching
182	    // removal, but that's a separate `Stream.multi`-wrapped subscription
183	    // that can land one microtask late, which previously left a one-frame
184	    // window where both the stale placeholder and the real confirmed
185	    // entry rendered at once.
186	    _pendingWrites = [
187	      for (final pending in _pendingWrites)
188	        if (pending.tempId != confirmation.tempId) pending,
189	    ];
190	    // Code-review fix: a confirmed entry that doesn't match the active
191	    // filter selection must never visibly violate it by appearing in the
192	    // list anyway.
193	    final matchesFilter = _matchesActiveFilters(
194	      source: entry.source,
195	      occurredAt: DateTime.parse(entry.occurredAt).toLocal(),
196	    );
197	    final current = state;
198	    if (current is MeusRegistrosLoaded) {
199	      // Prepended, not reloaded (Design Notes) — preserves this cubit's
200	      // own pagination state (`nextCursor`/`loadMoreFailed`) exactly as
201	      // `loadMore()`'s own cursor-overlap robustness already relies on;
202	      // `dedupedById` (unchanged) absorbs the degenerate case where a
203	      // later `list()`/`loadMore()` page's cursor also happens to repeat
204	      // this same (now server-known) id.
205	      emit(
206	        current.copyWith(
207	          entries: matchesFilter
208	              ? dedupedById([entry, ...current.entries], (e) => e.id)
209	              : current.entries,
210	          pendingWrites: _visiblePendingWrites,
211	        ),
212	      );

235	  /// `EntryRecordCard`'s own retry tap (`MeusRegistrosScreen`) — forwards
236	  /// to the shared tracker verbatim (Never: "a second retry endpoint").
237	  Future<void> retry(String tempId) => _tracker.retry(tempId);
238	
239	  /// `MeusRegistrosScreen.initState` calls this once, every mount — always
240	  /// re-fetches from scratch rather than keeping a previous visit's page
241	  /// around, since a new entry may have been saved (Insertion Modal, Epic
242	  /// 3) since the last visit. spec-5-2: also resets the filter selection
243	  /// to "none" first (a fresh mount's own "from scratch" promise extended
244	  /// to filters, Design Notes) — [_loadFiltered] then runs with that
245	  /// cleared selection, same as [clearFilters] would.
246	  Future<void> loadFirstPage() {
247	    _activeSource = null;
248	    _activeDateFrom = null;
249	    _activeDateTo = null;
250	    _activeDateRangePreset = DateRangePreset.allTime;
251	    return _loadFiltered();
252	  }

254	  /// `MeusRegistrosScreen`'s own `_ErrorState` retry button (code-review
255	  /// fix, spec-5-2) — unlike [loadFirstPage] (always resets to "no
256	  /// filters", for the fresh-mount case), this retries with whichever
257	  /// filter selection is still current. Review finding: wiring the error
258	  /// retry button to [loadFirstPage] silently dropped the active filter
259	  /// on retry — a failed *filtered* query would "succeed" by quietly
260	  /// showing the full unfiltered list instead of retrying the same
261	  /// filtered one.
262	  Future<void> retryCurrentPage() => _loadFiltered();
263	
264	  /// `EntriesFilterSheet`'s own "Aplicar" button (spec-5-2) — replaces
265	  /// whichever filters were active before with exactly [source]/
266	  /// [dateFrom]/[dateTo] (never merged with the previous selection: the
267	  /// active-filter chip row's own "x" already recomputes the full
268	  /// replacement set itself, passing back in every filter it wants kept —
269	  /// I/O matrix: "Remove one of two active chips"). Omitting a parameter
270	  /// clears that one filter dimension; omitting all three is equivalent to
271	  /// [clearFilters]. A separate method from [loadFirstPage] by design —
272	  /// see Design Notes — though both ultimately share [_loadFiltered]'s own
273	  /// "bump generation, replace state via list()" body.
274	  ///
275	  /// [dateRangePreset] (round-2 review fix) — the caller's own record of
276	  /// which [DateRangePreset] (if any) [dateFrom]/[dateTo] came from;
277	  /// defaults to [DateRangePreset.allTime], same "omitting clears it"
278	  /// convention as [dateFrom]/[dateTo] themselves. A caller re-applying an
279	  /// already-active date range verbatim (e.g. the chip row's own "remove
280	  /// just the source chip") must pass [activeDateRangePreset] back in
281	  /// explicitly to keep it from reverting to "Todo o período".
282	  Future<void> applyFilters({
283	    EntrySource? source,
284	    DateTime? dateFrom,
285	    DateTime? dateTo,
286	    DateRangePreset dateRangePreset = DateRangePreset.allTime,
287	  }) {
288	    _activeSource = source;
289	    _activeDateFrom = dateFrom;
290	    _activeDateTo = dateTo;
291	    _activeDateRangePreset = dateRangePreset;
292	    return _loadFiltered();
293	  }
294	
295	  /// The active-filter chip row's own "Limpar filtros" link (spec-5-2) —
296	  /// restores the full unfiltered list in place (I/O matrix: "Clear all
297	  /// filters"), without a screen reload/re-mount.
298	  Future<void> clearFilters() {
299	    _activeSource = null;
300	    _activeDateFrom = null;
301	    _activeDateTo = null;
302	    _activeDateRangePreset = DateRangePreset.allTime;
303	    return _loadFiltered();
304	  }
305	
306	  /// [loadFirstPage]/[applyFilters]/[clearFilters]'s own shared "bump
307	  /// generation, replace state via list()" body — always queries
308	  /// whichever filter selection ([_activeSource]/[_activeDateFrom]/
309	  /// [_activeDateTo]) is current at call time, cursor-less (always a
310	  /// fresh first page, never a continuation — [_fetchMore] is the one
311	  /// path that ever passes a cursor).
312	  Future<void> _loadFiltered() async {
313	    final generation = ++_generation;
314	    emit(const MeusRegistrosLoading());
315	    final result = await _repository.list(
316	      source: _activeSource,
317	      dateFrom: _activeDateFrom,
318	      dateTo: _activeDateTo,
319	    );
320	    // Mirrors `AccountSettingsCubit.toggleBiometric`'s own guard: `close()`
321	    // can race this awaited call (e.g. a fast app teardown mid-request) —
322	    // `emit()` after `close()` would otherwise throw.
323	    if (isClosed || generation != _generation) {
324	      return;
325	    }
326	    result.match(
327	      (failure) {
328	        // Review finding (round 2): mirrors the success branch's own
329	        // `_pendingWrites` overlay below — a write already pending/failed
330	        // when the first page fails to load must still show its own
331	        // placeholder card, not disappear behind a plain error screen
332	        // until the next unrelated `pendingWrites` emission. Gated on
333	        // `_visiblePendingWrites` (code-review fix, spec-5-2): a pending
334	        // write that doesn't match the active filter selection has
335	        // nothing to show here either.
336	        final visiblePendingWrites = _visiblePendingWrites;
337	        if (visiblePendingWrites.isEmpty) {
338	          emit(MeusRegistrosError(message: failure.message));
339	          return;
340	        }
341	        emit(
342	          MeusRegistrosLoaded(
343	            entries: const [],
344	            nextCursor: null,
345	            pendingWrites: visiblePendingWrites,
346	          ),
347	        );
348	      },
349	      (page) {
350	        // Same degenerate-cursor distrust as `_fetchMore`'s own guard below:
351	        // a page reporting zero items is treated as exhausted regardless of
352	        // `page.nextCursor` — an empty first page with a non-null cursor
353	        // would otherwise strand the user on `MeusRegistrosEmpty` with no
354	        // way back to a cursor this state no longer tracks. Forced
355	        // unconditionally (Review finding, round 1): independent of
356	        // `_pendingWrites` below — a pending write outstanding over an
357	        // otherwise-empty first page must still null out the cursor, not
358	        // just skip the `MeusRegistrosEmpty` branch beneath it.
359	        final nextCursor = page.items.isEmpty ? null : page.nextCursor;
360	        // spec-4-2: a pending write already outstanding still needs its
361	        // own placeholder card to show, even over an otherwise-empty first
362	        // page — skips straight to `MeusRegistrosEmpty` only once neither
363	        // applies. Gated on `_visiblePendingWrites` (code-review fix,
364	        // spec-5-2), same rationale as the failure branch above.
365	        final visiblePendingWrites = _visiblePendingWrites;
366	        if (page.items.isEmpty && visiblePendingWrites.isEmpty) {
367	          emit(const MeusRegistrosEmpty());
368	          return;
369	        }
370	        emit(
371	          MeusRegistrosLoaded(
372	            entries: dedupedById(page.items, (entry) => entry.id),
373	            nextCursor: nextCursor,
374	            pendingWrites: visiblePendingWrites,
375	          ),
376	        );
377	      },
378	    );
379	  }
380	
381	  /// `MeusRegistrosScreen`'s scroll listener calls this near the list's
382	  /// end. A no-op while not [MeusRegistrosLoaded], while
383	  /// [MeusRegistrosLoaded.nextCursor] is already `null`, while a call is
384	  /// already in flight, or — critically — once
385	  /// [MeusRegistrosLoaded.loadMoreFailed] is already `true`: without that
386	  /// last guard, a failed page's own footer swapping from a spinner to a
387	  /// "Tentar novamente" button can shift the list's `maxScrollExtent`
388	  /// just enough to leave the scroll position still inside the
389	  /// pre-fetch-buffer zone, re-firing this same listener and retrying
390	  /// forever — observed directly as an unbounded `pumpAndSettle` loop in
391	  /// this screen's own widget test. Once failed, only an explicit
392	  /// [retryLoadMore] (the footer's own button) tries again.
393	  Future<void> loadMore() => _fetchMore(isRetry: false);
394	
395	  /// The footer's "Tentar novamente" button — the one path allowed to
396	  /// retry past a [MeusRegistrosLoaded.loadMoreFailed] of `true`
397	  /// ([loadMore]'s own doc).
398	  Future<void> retryLoadMore() => _fetchMore(isRetry: true);
399	
400	  Future<void> _fetchMore({required bool isRetry}) async {
401	    final current = state;
402	    if (current is! MeusRegistrosLoaded ||
403	        current.nextCursor == null ||
404	        current.isLoadingMore ||
405	        (current.loadMoreFailed && !isRetry)) {
406	      return;
407	    }
408	    final generation = _generation;
409	    emit(current.copyWith(isLoadingMore: true, loadMoreFailed: false));
410	    // spec-5-2 I/O matrix: "Load more with filters active" — the
411	    // continuation carries the exact same filter selection as whichever
412	    // `_loadFiltered()` call fetched this page's own first page.
413	    final result = await _repository.list(
414	      cursor: current.nextCursor,
415	      source: _activeSource,
416	      dateFrom: _activeDateFrom,
417	      dateTo: _activeDateTo,
418	    );
419	    if (isClosed || generation != _generation) {
420	      return;
421	    }
422	    // Re-reads `state` rather than closing over `current` — defensive
423	    // against `loadFirstPage()` having reset the state to something other
424	    // than `MeusRegistrosLoaded` while this await was pending.
425	    final latest = state;
426	    if (latest is! MeusRegistrosLoaded) {
427	      return;
428	    }
429	    result.match(
430	      (failure) =>
431	          emit(latest.copyWith(isLoadingMore: false, loadMoreFailed: true)),
432	      (page) {
433	        // I/O matrix: "Next page appended, no dup ids" — defensive
434	        // de-duplication in case a cursor-boundary entry is ever repeated
435	        // by the server, including a repeat *within* this same page
436	        // (`dedupedById`'s running `seenIds` set covers both).
437	        final seenIds = latest.entries.map((entry) => entry.id).toSet();
438	        final newEntries = dedupedById(
439	          page.items,
440	          (entry) => entry.id,
441	          seenIds: seenIds,
442	        );
443	        // Defensive guard against a degenerate server response: if every
444	        // item in this "successful" page was already present by id (zero
445	        // genuinely-new entries) yet the server still reports a non-null
446	        // `nextCursor`, treat the page as exhausted rather than trusting
447	        // that cursor — otherwise a misbehaving/stuck server cursor could
448	        // make the scroll listener keep re-triggering `loadMore()`
449	        // indefinitely with no progress.
450	        final nextCursor = newEntries.isEmpty ? null : page.nextCursor;
451	        emit(
452	          MeusRegistrosLoaded(
453	            entries: [...latest.entries, ...newEntries],
454	            nextCursor: nextCursor,
455	            pendingWrites: latest.pendingWrites,
456	          ),
457	        );
458	      },
459	    );
460	  }
461	
462	  @override
463	  Future<void> close() async {
464	    await _pendingSubscription.cancel();
465	    await _confirmedSubscription.cancel();
466	    return super.close();
467	  }
468	}

# Cerne — Requirements and Screen Flow

Cerne is a reflective-journaling mobile app with an AI assistant. The user records their day by text, audio or photo; a conversational agent consults those records (semantic search) to answer with context and to offer insights.

This document is the product specification. The visual reference is the prototype in `docs/input/prototype/`; the backend API is documented in `docs/input/backend/`.

---

## 1. Functional requirements

### RF01 — Multimodal capture (text / audio / photo)
Data entry by text, real-time audio recording and photo upload — always through Screen 2 (Insertion Modal), which has a raw text field in addition to the microphone and the gallery. Every capture becomes a persisted record (`POST /entries`), **distinct from a chat message** (see the separation note in RF04).

**Acceptance criteria:**
- The three modalities (text, audio, photo) result in the same persisted-entry format — none is treated structurally differently from the others after capture.
- Cancelling a capture midway (e.g., interrupting a recording) does not create a partial or empty entry.

### RF02 — Speech-to-text / OCR processing
Transcription of audio (speech-to-text) and recognition of text in images (OCR) over the content captured in RF01.

**Acceptance criteria:** four visible states — recording, processing, transcribed, transcription error.

### RF03 — Biometric authentication vault
Access barrier via Face ID / Touch ID / PIN before exposing the user's data.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- A biometric failure (e.g., fingerprint not recognized) offers PIN as an alternative, without locking the user out of the app.
- The app, sent to the background and resumed after 5 minutes, requires authentication again — it does not stay unlocked indefinitely (fixed value, not configurable by the user).

### RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG)
Continuous conversation with the AI agent, with semantic search over previous entries. **Chat messages are conversational and do not create journal entries automatically** — the only exception is the explicit save action described in RF10. Otherwise, the chat queries existing entries via RAG but does not write to them.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Three mandatory UI states: processing/streaming, error, complete response.
- If the response stream drops midway, the partial message stays visible with a failure indication (it does not disappear).

### RF05 — Personal summary export
Generation of a narrative summary by AI (Claude Haiku 4.5) from the user's entries, exportable as PDF, with an additional option to download the raw data without the narrative. No clinical or diagnostic connotation. **Scope: job generation, file download and failure handling — never the quality of the generated narrative text.**

**Acceptance criteria:**
- An export job with zero entries in the period returns a handled error state (not an empty PDF, not a crash).
- A failure generating the narrative text (model timeout) still allows downloading the raw data without the narrative — the export is not blocked by an AI failure.

### RF06 — Semantic search / filter over journal entries
Semantic similarity search (via Voyage AI embeddings, reusing the ones already generated in RF01) combined with metadata filters (date, entry type). There is no filter by tag or category: the backend does not implement it in any endpoint — `GET /entries` and `GET /entries/search` accept only `source` and `dateFrom`/`dateTo`. Tags appear only embedded, read-only, in the `Entry` object (see section 2).

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Searching for a term finds semantically related entries even without the exact word (e.g., searching "ansiedade" returns an entry that only mentions "nervosismo", without the literal term).
- 300 ms search debounce: fast typing triggers a single query, not one per keystroke.
- Results from the local read cache stay consistent with the server after reconnection, without duplicating displayed items *(the architecture is cloud-only; offline allows only viewing already-cached data, not writing)*.
- Two or more filters applied at the same time (`source` + `dateFrom`/`dateTo`) narrow results with AND logic (not OR).
- Clearing the filters returns to the full list without restarting the screen.

### RF07 — Multi-source history (timeline)
A screen whose state depends simultaneously on authentication, synchronization status and entry data.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Session expiration while viewing triggers a new-login prompt without a crash and without losing the scroll position.
- The per-entry synchronization status badge updates independently of the authentication stream.
- No BLoC imports another BLoC directly.

### RF08 — Proactive insights (mechanism)
A suggestion inserted into the chat without the user asking for it. **Scope: only the trigger mechanism, never the quality of the generated text.**

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Trigger after N = 5 user messages OR T = 2 min of inactivity — fires exactly once per satisfied condition.
- If insight generation fails (timeout / network error), the main chat keeps working normally.
- Dismissing the insight does not change the scroll position or the state of the main conversation.

### RF09 — Temporal summaries / dashboard
An evolution chart with a textual summary, computed on demand when the Settings tab is opened. **Scope: aggregation and rendering, never the quality of the narrative text.**

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Renders correctly in three scenarios: zero entries, one entry, more than 30 entries.
- The aggregation recalculates correctly after an entry is created (cache-invalidation test). Entries are immutable: there is no `PATCH /entries/:id` or `DELETE /entries/:id` in the backend, and no screen describes an edit or delete action on an entry.
- The AI narrative text is checked only for not breaking the UI in extreme cases — never for its content.

### RF10 — Save a chat message as an entry
A button on each user message in the chat that converts it into a persisted entry — for moments when the user states relevant information during the conversation, not only through dedicated capture (RF01). It reuses the same `POST /entries` pipeline (PII check + embedding), with the origin marked as `chat`.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- The chat feature triggers the creation of the entry through a shared interface / use case, never by directly importing a repository or data source of the entries feature — a violation here also breaks RNF06.
- Saving the same message twice does not create duplicate entries (idempotency).
- A failure to save (network unavailable) keeps the conversation working normally, and the button returns to a state that allows trying again — the same failure-isolation pattern as RF08.
- Only user messages have the button — AI responses cannot become entries.

---

## 2. Extension features — not implemented

1	/// INTERVALO DE DATA's own 3 choices (spec-5-2; `prototype-extract.md`) —
2	/// each computes its own `dateFrom`/`dateTo` pair via [rangeFrom]. [allTime]
3	/// is itself a selectable choice meaning "no date filter at all", not some
4	/// maximal range — it resolves to `(null, null)`.
5	///
6	/// Lives in the domain layer (RNF06) rather than alongside
7	/// `EntriesFilterSheet` so `MeusRegistrosCubit` can store the selected
8	/// preset directly (code-review fix: re-deriving it from `dateFrom` by
9	/// equality match against a freshly recomputed "today" boundary goes stale
10	/// the moment a day/week/month boundary rolls over while the filter stays
11	/// active) without the cubit importing a presentation-layer widget file.
12	/// UI-facing copy (`label`) stays out of this enum, same split
13	/// `EntrySource`/`entrySourceLabel` already uses — see
14	/// `entries_filter_sheet.dart`'s own `dateRangePresetLabel`.
15	enum DateRangePreset {
16	  allTime,
17	  thisWeek,
18	  thisMonth;
19	
20	  /// This preset's own `(dateFrom, dateTo)` pair, anchored to [now] (a
21	  /// parameter only so a test can pin it — every real call site passes
22	  /// `DateTime.now()`). `dateTo` is always [now] itself — "through right
23	  /// now" — `docs/input/` is silent on inclusive/exclusive bounds here
24	  /// (AGENTS.md policy: "decide and proceed"). `dateFrom` is local
25	  /// midnight of the Monday starting this week, or the 1st of this
26	  /// calendar month.
27	  (DateTime?, DateTime?) rangeFrom(DateTime now) {
28	    final today = DateTime(now.year, now.month, now.day);
29	    switch (this) {
30	      case DateRangePreset.allTime:
31	        return (null, null);
32	      case DateRangePreset.thisWeek:
33	        return (today.subtract(Duration(days: today.weekday - 1)), now);
34	      case DateRangePreset.thisMonth:
35	        return (DateTime(today.year, today.month), now);
36	    }
37	  }
38	}

---
title: 'Combined Search + Filter & Non-Disruptive Clearing'
type: 'feature'
created: '2026-11-05'
status: 'draft'
review_loop_iteration: 0
context: []
baseline_commit: 'afb4d317b6cdd39d6fbf4d87943e5e0aae51da05'
---

<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** `EntriesSearchCubit` (5.1) and `MeusRegistrosCubit`'s filters (5.2) are fully wired but mutually inert — applying/clearing a filter while a search term is active silently updates hidden cubit state with zero visible effect, and a search query never carries the active filter at all.

**Approach:** Give `EntriesSearchCubit` its own filter fields plus an `updateFilters()` entry point; have `MeusRegistrosScreen` (the only place that already composes both cubits) call it alongside every existing filter-mutating call, and have `_search()` forward those fields to `entries-search`. Clearing/removing a filter while a search is active re-runs the same search term with the new filter set in place — no query-box change, no screen reload.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- `EntriesRepository.search({required String query, EntrySource? source, DateTime? dateFrom, DateTime? dateTo})`; `EntriesRemoteDataSource.search()` forwards non-null values as `source`(`.name`)/`dateFrom`/`dateTo` (`.toUtc().toIso8601String()`) to `entries-search`, mirroring `list()`'s own convention exactly.
- `EntriesSearchCubit` gains `_activeSource`/`_activeDateFrom`/`_activeDateTo` (same "`null` = no filter of that kind" convention as `MeusRegistrosCubit`) plus `updateFilters({source, dateFrom, dateTo})`: stores them always; additionally, only when a query is currently active (tracked via a new `_lastQuery` field, non-empty), cancels any pending debounce `Timer` and immediately re-runs `_search(_lastQuery)` with the new filters, bumping `_generation` exactly as `_search`'s own race-guard already requires. While idle, storage is silent — no network call, no state change.
- `_search(query)` passes `source: _activeSource, dateFrom: _activeDateFrom, dateTo: _activeDateTo` to `_repository.search()` alongside `query`.
- `MeusRegistrosScreen` threads `searchCubit` into `EntriesFilterSheet` and `_ActiveFiltersRow` (new required constructor param on both); every one of their 4 existing filter-mutating calls (`_applyAndClose`, chip-remove ×2, "Limpar filtros") also calls `searchCubit.updateFilters(...)` with the exact resulting source/dateFrom/dateTo, right after the existing `cubit.applyFilters()`/`clearFilters()` call.
- Funnel "filled" indicator (`meus_registros_screen.dart:217-219`) drops its `searchState is ResourceIdle` gate — becomes unconditionally `widget.cubit.hasActiveFilters`.
- `_ActiveFiltersRow` renders above `_SearchResults` too (not only the plain-timeline branch) whenever `widget.cubit.hasActiveFilters` is true, independent of `searchState`.
- Clearing the search box (empty query) while filters stay active needs no new code: `MeusRegistrosCubit`'s own filtered state is already kept current in the background regardless of which branch is visible (unchanged 5.2 behavior).

**Ask First:** none — scope pinned by `epic-5-context.md` and RF06.

**Never:** `EntriesSearchCubit` importing `MeusRegistrosCubit` or vice versa (RNF06) — filters flow only through the screen-mediated `updateFilters()` call; a debounce on the filter-triggered re-search (only keystrokes debounce, Boundaries already settled in 5.1); a "CATEGORIA"/tag filter (extension, forbidden); changing `MeusRegistrosCubit._loadFiltered()`'s own `entries-list` background query, which keeps running exactly as 5.2 left it even while hidden behind active search results.

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Apply filter during active search | search "ansiedade" active, Aplicar "áudio" | one `entries-search` call: `q=ansiedade&source=audio`, AND narrowing | N/A |
| Clear filters during active search | source+date active alongside a search term, "Limpar filtros" tapped | re-queries `entries-search` with only `q`; search box/text untouched, no reload | N/A |
| Remove one of two chips during active search | source+date active, search active, "x" on source chip | re-queries `entries-search` with `q` + remaining date range only | N/A |
| Apply filter while search idle | empty search box, Aplicar "áudio" | stored on `EntriesSearchCubit` silently; `entries-list` queried (unchanged 5.2 path), no `entries-search` call | N/A |
| Clear search box with filters active | search cleared to empty, filters still active | falls back to `MeusRegistrosCubit`'s already-current filtered list, no new network call | N/A |

</frozen-after-approval>

## Code Map

- `entries_repository.dart:88` -- `search()` signature to extend with `source`/`dateFrom`/`dateTo`
- `entries_remote_data_source.dart:125-143` -- `search()` query-param building to extend, mirroring `list()`'s own (lines 65-96)
- `entries_repository_impl.dart:135-136` -- thin pass-through, no change beyond the new params
- `entries_search_cubit.dart:20-100` -- add filter fields + `_lastQuery` + `updateFilters()`; extend `_search()`'s repository call and set/clear `_lastQuery` in `onQueryChanged`
- `meus_registros_screen.dart:208-223` (funnel fill gate), `:260-282` (chip-row branch, currently plain-timeline-only), `:656-710` (`_ActiveFiltersRow`, needs `searchCubit` param)
- `entries_filter_sheet.dart:38-96,121-130` (`EntriesFilterSheet`/`_applyAndClose`, needs `searchCubit` param + bridging call)
- `meus_registros_cubit.dart` -- unchanged; `activeSource`/`activeDateFrom`/`activeDateTo`/`activeDateRangePreset` getters reused read-only for the bridge
- `date_range_preset.dart` -- unchanged, reused as-is

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**

---
title: 'Combined Search + Filter & Non-Disruptive Clearing'
type: 'feature'
created: '2026-11-05'
status: 'draft'
review_loop_iteration: 0
context: []
baseline_commit: 'afb4d317b6cdd39d6fbf4d87943e5e0aae51da05'
---

<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** `EntriesSearchCubit` (5.1) and `MeusRegistrosCubit`'s filters (5.2) are fully wired but mutually inert — applying/clearing a filter while a search term is active silently updates hidden cubit state with zero visible effect, and a search query never carries the active filter at all.

**Approach:** Give `EntriesSearchCubit` its own filter fields plus an `updateFilters()` entry point; have `MeusRegistrosScreen` (the only place that already composes both cubits) call it alongside every existing filter-mutating call, and have `_search()` forward those fields to `entries-search`. Clearing/removing a filter while a search is active re-runs the same search term with the new filter set in place — no query-box change, no screen reload.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- `EntriesRepository.search({required String query, EntrySource? source, DateTime? dateFrom, DateTime? dateTo})`; `EntriesRemoteDataSource.search()` forwards non-null values as `source`(`.name`)/`dateFrom`/`dateTo` (`.toUtc().toIso8601String()`) to `entries-search`, mirroring `list()`'s own convention exactly.
- `EntriesSearchCubit` gains `_activeSource`/`_activeDateFrom`/`_activeDateTo` (same "`null` = no filter of that kind" convention as `MeusRegistrosCubit`) plus `updateFilters({source, dateFrom, dateTo})`: stores them always; additionally, only when a query is currently active (tracked via a new `_lastQuery` field, non-empty), cancels any pending debounce `Timer` and immediately re-runs `_search(_lastQuery)` with the new filters, bumping `_generation` exactly as `_search`'s own race-guard already requires. While idle, storage is silent — no network call, no state change.
- `_search(query)` passes `source: _activeSource, dateFrom: _activeDateFrom, dateTo: _activeDateTo` to `_repository.search()` alongside `query`.
- `MeusRegistrosScreen` threads `searchCubit` into `EntriesFilterSheet` and `_ActiveFiltersRow` (new required constructor param on both); every one of their 4 existing filter-mutating calls (`_applyAndClose`, chip-remove ×2, "Limpar filtros") also calls `searchCubit.updateFilters(...)` with the exact resulting source/dateFrom/dateTo, right after the existing `cubit.applyFilters()`/`clearFilters()` call.
- Funnel "filled" indicator (`meus_registros_screen.dart:217-219`) drops its `searchState is ResourceIdle` gate — becomes unconditionally `widget.cubit.hasActiveFilters`.
- `_ActiveFiltersRow` renders above `_SearchResults` too (not only the plain-timeline branch) whenever `widget.cubit.hasActiveFilters` is true, independent of `searchState`.
- Clearing the search box (empty query) while filters stay active needs no new code: `MeusRegistrosCubit`'s own filtered state is already kept current in the background regardless of which branch is visible (unchanged 5.2 behavior).

**Ask First:** none — scope pinned by `epic-5-context.md` and RF06.

**Never:** `EntriesSearchCubit` importing `MeusRegistrosCubit` or vice versa (RNF06) — filters flow only through the screen-mediated `updateFilters()` call; a debounce on the filter-triggered re-search (only keystrokes debounce, Boundaries already settled in 5.1); a "CATEGORIA"/tag filter (extension, forbidden); changing `MeusRegistrosCubit._loadFiltered()`'s own `entries-list` background query, which keeps running exactly as 5.2 left it even while hidden behind active search results.

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Apply filter during active search | search "ansiedade" active, Aplicar "áudio" | one `entries-search` call: `q=ansiedade&source=audio`, AND narrowing | N/A |
| Clear filters during active search | source+date active alongside a search term, "Limpar filtros" tapped | re-queries `entries-search` with only `q`; search box/text untouched, no reload | N/A |
| Remove one of two chips during active search | source+date active, search active, "x" on source chip | re-queries `entries-search` with `q` + remaining date range only | N/A |
| Apply filter while search idle | empty search box, Aplicar "áudio" | stored on `EntriesSearchCubit` silently; `entries-list` queried (unchanged 5.2 path), no `entries-search` call | N/A |
| Clear search box with filters active | search cleared to empty, filters still active | falls back to `MeusRegistrosCubit`'s already-current filtered list, no new network call | N/A |

</frozen-after-approval>

## Code Map

- `entries_repository.dart:88` -- `search()` signature to extend with `source`/`dateFrom`/`dateTo`
- `entries_remote_data_source.dart:125-143` -- `search()` query-param building to extend, mirroring `list()`'s own (lines 65-96)
- `entries_repository_impl.dart:135-136` -- thin pass-through, no change beyond the new params
- `entries_search_cubit.dart:20-100` -- add filter fields + `_lastQuery` + `updateFilters()`; extend `_search()`'s repository call and set/clear `_lastQuery` in `onQueryChanged`
- `meus_registros_screen.dart:208-223` (funnel fill gate), `:260-282` (chip-row branch, currently plain-timeline-only), `:656-710` (`_ActiveFiltersRow`, needs `searchCubit` param)
- `entries_filter_sheet.dart:38-96,121-130` (`EntriesFilterSheet`/`_applyAndClose`, needs `searchCubit` param + bridging call)
- `meus_registros_cubit.dart` -- unchanged; `activeSource`/`activeDateFrom`/`activeDateTo`/`activeDateRangePreset` getters reused read-only for the bridge
- `date_range_preset.dart` -- unchanged, reused as-is

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**
- [ ] `entries_repository.dart` -- add `source`/`dateFrom`/`dateTo` params to `search()`
- [ ] `entries_remote_data_source.dart` -- forward new params to `entries-search`, mirroring `list()`'s UTC-serialization convention
- [ ] `entries_search_cubit.dart` -- add filter fields, `_lastQuery`, `updateFilters()`; wire into `_search()`
- [ ] `entries_filter_sheet.dart` -- add `searchCubit` param; `_applyAndClose` bridges both cubits
- [ ] `meus_registros_screen.dart` -- pass `searchCubit` to `EntriesFilterSheet`/`_ActiveFiltersRow`; bridge both chip-remove sites + "Limpar filtros"; drop the funnel's `ResourceIdle` gate; render `_ActiveFiltersRow` above search results too
- [ ] Unit tests covering every I/O Matrix row across the new/changed files
- [ ] Widget tests: chip row + funnel fill rendered during an active search; Aplicar/Limpar/chip-remove during active search re-querying `entries-search` with the right params

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given an active search term and no filters, when a filter is applied via "Aplicar", then the funnel fills and the chip row appears above the search results.
- Given combined search+filter results on screen, when "Limpar filtros" is tapped, then results update to the unfiltered semantic-search results for the same query, with the search box and screen left otherwise undisturbed.
- Given a search term and filters both active, when the user scrolls (plain-timeline-only `loadMore()` is a no-op here since search results aren't paginated), then no `entries-list` call fires from that scroll.

## Design Notes

Filter state is duplicated (not shared) between `MeusRegistrosCubit` and `EntriesSearchCubit` by design — RNF06 forbids one BLoC importing the other, so `MeusRegistrosScreen`, which already composes both as sibling `BlocProvider.value`s, is the only legitimate place to copy a filter change from one cubit's call site into the other's `updateFilters()`.

`entries-search`'s own `limit` cap (50, no `cursor`) is unchanged by this story — combining filters never introduces pagination into search results.

## Verification

**Commands:**
- `fvm flutter analyze` -- expected: zero issues
- `fvm flutter test` -- expected: all tests pass
